newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast products steady against easing NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast products steady against easing NYMEX.

text.p: Bouyed by an outage at a key regional refinery, U.S. West Coast spot products prices were steady against a sharp drop in NYMEX futures prices, traders said Wednesday.
But trade was thin as the market monitored a sell-off in NYMEX unleaded and heating oil futures that sent prices sharply lower on the day and pushed West Coast players to the sidelines.

January unleaded gasoline bottomed out at 62.80 cents a gallon in NYMEX trade before recovering to settle at 63.56, down 3.3 cents on the day. January heating oil sank to 66.40 cents a gallon before ending down 2.8 cents at 66.82 cents.
Unocal confirmed a hydrocracker was taken off line over the weekend at its 130,000 barrel per day Los Angeles-area refinery, which produces 75,000 barrels per day of gasoline.
Traders said Unocal appeared to have covered its positions and was out of the market. "Unocal has kind of backed out of it," one trader said.
Low sulphur diesel was heard done at 67.25 cents a gallon, but offers moved 0.25 cent lower on a lack of buyers later in the day.
Regular unleaded firmed 0.50 cent a gallon to 67 cents a gallon bid, 68 cents asked in Los Angeles and the Bay Area.
